n0.hypothesis: Reproducible posterior scores and scene-region weights at minimum measured compute cost; baseline fails convergence, no candidate is accepted without held-out replication.
n0.insight:
[from n3] Proposal density and support must be explicit before using measurement-informed starts for reference weights. Proposal quality must be measured independently.
[from n2] Assess complete independent populations on the normalizer scale; particle count and weight ESS cannot stand in for convergence.
[from n4] Use independent full-population score and normalizer variation to judge progress; a gradual schedule can make every incremental ESS look healthy despite a poorly explored posterior.
[from n5] Check movement at the posterior temperature separately from the annealing average. Changing initial tails cannot by itself repair an ill-scaled final kernel.
[from n6] For strongly heterogeneous or mixed posteriors, a global pilot covariance can overestimate narrow local directions. Test geometry with independent score replication, not covariance plausibility or acceptance averages.
[from n7] Correct global scene proposals still need demonstrated mode access and stable weights. Diagnose target/environment support and proposal-density cost before increasing their mixture frequency.
[from n9] Keep legitimate zero-mass realizations and their replicate denominator; unknown failures must remain errors. No-redraw behavior needs end-to-end tests, not only an aggregation helper.
[from n8] Useful final-temperature movement does not guarantee stable annealing normalizers. Independently test proposal-to-posterior distance and early loss of particle diversity.
[from n11] Informed scene initialization requires a normalized native point law and the true numerical Poisson intensity, including explicit singular-support accounting. A generic density-ratio identity alone does not supply a usable sampler.
[from n14] Known-density scene proposals require the numerical native mark measure itself, not merely an analytic-support correction. Account separately for support slivers, zero-target initial draws, and genuine generator failures.
[from n13] Local geometry and a normalized joint proposal solve different problems: local movement can improve while whole-population normalizing mass stays unstable. Test the combination with independent pilots, changed proposals and increased effort, then on untouched observations including all preparation costs.
[from n15] Remove analytically known zero-mean score fluctuations for diagnosis as well as efficiency: a raw comparison can pass because its noise is too large to expose a smaller systematic discrepancy. Preserve failed original checks and predeclare repaired numerical validation.
[from n14] Endpoint equality is not kernel validity: the old native exchange omitted the numerical lower-uniform support bound. Real allowed prior marks demonstrate a zero-environment-density swap. Correct every caller, and require corrected runs or full trajectory evidence before interpreting old proposal/effort comparisons as same-target convergence.
